children: Shares are trading below their IPO price of $83 on Tuesday, less than a week after their debut on the Nasdaq
Anthropic shares debuted on the Nasdaq last week at a big premium, but they've have quickly fallen below the stock's IPO price.
Anthropic has officially broken below its initial-public-offering price for the first time, after the stock missed out Monday on the Nvidia-fueled rally that started the week on Wall Street.

Anthropic shares (ANT) traded as low as $75.61 on Tuesday, below the IPO price of $83. Anthropic's losses briefly pushed its market capitalization to $999.5 billion, below the $1 trillion mark for the first time, according to Dow Jones Market Data. Before its IPO, Anthropic was valued at $965 billion.
While the stock slightly recovered Tuesday afternoon, it was still trading well below its $115.10 peak achieved last Thursday following the company's record-breaking offering.

It's never great when newly public stocks dip below their IPO prices, and Anthropic's fall to Earth has been quick. For example, it took SpaceX shares (SPCX) about a month to break below their IPO price.

The troubles for Anthropic as a new publicly traded company coincide with fresh cracks in the artificial-intelligence trade, the aftermath of recent U.S. midterm elections and the fallout at Nvidia (NVDA) following CEO Jensen Huang's resignation and reinstatement. Huang returned to the company on Monday, lifting shares of Nvidia and much of the AI sector, - but not Anthropic.

On Tuesday, Axios reported that Anthropic and archrival OpenAI are developing new AI models powerful enough that some staff don't believe they can be safely released to the public. Both companies have called for pacing AI development and have said they are working with third parties to evaluate their models.

"The models are now capable enough that we need to think about safety, security, alignment," OpenAI President Greg Brockman said at a conference last week. "It's not any one company. It's really a whole industrywide shift."

An Anthropic spokesperson said in a statement that the company "recently" delayed pretraining a new frontier model for more than a month to give it time to bolster its security. "The hardest safety work is still ahead, and we've been clear that we may slow down or hold back even when it costs us," the spokesperson said.
OpenAI did not immediately return a request for comment.

Wall Street is expressing confidence in Anthropic's long-term trajectory despite the turbulence. All but two of the 15 analysts covering the company have a buy rating on the stock, according to FactSet. That includes Canaccord Genuity, Wedbush and Oppenheimer, each of which initiated coverage of Anthropic this week.

Wedbush analyst Ygal Arounian on Monday acknowledged that Anthropic went public in a "tumultuous market" but said that the AI ecosystem will continue to be built. "The genie is out of the bottle. And [Anthropic] is a strong play on that theme," Arounian wrote in a client note. His $120-a-share price target implies a 50% hike from current levels.

Retail investors have also continued to buy the stock. According to Vanda Research, retail net buying of Anthropic shares has risen as the price has fallen, reaching more than $100 million on Monday. Anthropic was the second-most bought stock among individual investors on Monday, Vanda data showed.

"Overall enthusiasm for [Anthropic] has been on par with [Nvidia] in recent sessions, signaling that the stock is very much a 'retail favorite' already," Viraj Patel, a global macro strategist at Vanda, said in a Monday report.
